title: Ohio's 13th Congressional District General Election, 2026
description: The general election for Ohio's 13th Congressional District pits two-term Democratic incumbent Emilia Sykes against Republican nominee Carey Coleman, a former radio talk show host and television meteorologist. The district was redrawn in October 2025 by the Ohio Redistricting Commission and now leans Democratic (Cook Partisan Voting Index D+2; Cook Political Report rating Lean D), after previously being considered a toss-up. Sykes defeated Republican Kevin Coughlin by 51.1% in 2024, and the new map prompted Coughlin to withdraw from the 2026 race. The contest will test whether national midterm trends and Republican messaging on the economy and border security can overcome the district's Democratic tilt.
polling_note: No public opinion polls specific to the Sykes–Coleman general election matchup were found as of June 2026. Prediction markets and election forecasters (Cook Political Report, 270toWin) rate the race as Lean Democratic.

candidates.name: Emilia Sykes
candidates.summary: Emilia Sykes is the incumbent U.S. Representative for Ohio's 13th Congressional District, first elected in 2022. She previously served eight years in the Ohio House of Representatives, including three years as House Minority Leader. In Congress, she serves on the Transportation and Infrastructure and Science, Space, and Technology committees and has focused on lowering costs, protecting Medicare and Social Security, and securing federal funding for her district.

candidates.name: Carey Coleman
candidates.summary: Carey Coleman is a former radio talk show host on WNIR-FM in Akron and a former television meteorologist who worked at WKYC-TV and WOIO-TV in Cleveland, as well as The Weather Channel and CNN. He won a five-way Republican primary on May 5, 2026, to become the GOP nominee. Coleman emphasizes fiscal discipline, border security, energy independence, and conservative values in his campaign.
